clinical_features.symptoms:
signs/ECG are significantly abnormal 
• 
Rapid ABC assessment 
• 
IV access only if patient unstable 
• 
Bedside investigations: HGT, VBG, urine ß-HCG for all females 
• 
ECG on all patients – look for features of ischaemia, prolonged QT interval, shortened PR interval 
or ECG signs of metabolic derangements (see Protocol: ECG for causes of syncope) 
• 
Correct electrolyte abnormalities 
• 
Comprehensive history including collateral and thorough physical examination 
■ 
Focused CVS and CNS examination 
■ 
Complete head to toe examination 
• 
Further investigations: FBC, U&E, D-dimer, serial troponins and ECGs as indicated, 
• 
POCUS – AAA, ectopic, volume status, cardiac contractility/structural abnormalities. 
• 
CT Brain if neurological fallout 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
Cardiovascular & Respiratory 
CAUSES 
Up to 50% - no cause found in ED 
■ 
Dysrhythmias: AV nodal blocks/Paroxysmal SVT/VT/AF, pacemaker dysfx 
■ 
Hereditary syndromes e.g. WPW, Brugada, ARVC, long/short QT, obstructive cardiomyopathy 
■ 
Structural heart disease e.g. aortic stenosis, obstructive cardiomyopathy 
■ 
ACS, especially RV infarction 
■ 
Aortic dissection 
■ 
Pericardial tamponade 
■ 
PE 
■ 
Vascular steal syndromes 
• 
Orthostatic 
■ 
Autonomic failure: pure autonomic failure, diabetic neuropathy, Parkinson’s, drugs/ETOH 
■ 
Volume depletion: haemorrhage (NB ECTOPIC PREGNANCY), diarrhoea, Addison’s disease 
• 
Neurally-mediated 
■ 
Vasovagal faint – prolonged standing, warm environment, stressors, pain, anxiety 
■ 
Situational: cough, sneeze, micturition, defaecation, exercise related, carotid sinus pressure 
■ 
Carotid sinus syncope 
 
 
HIGH RISK CLINICAL FEATURES 
•
Extremes of age 
•
Documented or suspected cardiac abnormalities/ischaemia 
•
Diabetes 
•
Recurrent, frequent syncopal episodes without clear cause 
•
Anaemia/suspected haemorrhage – ectopic, GI bleed 
•
Persistent abnormal vital signs 
•
Syncope during exertion - HOCM 
•
Family hx of sudden death – hereditary cardiac syndromes 
 
DI
